subject: Stratus AI dedicated onramp & slab sizing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Li Wei <li.wei@stratus.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-01T08:57:00-07:00
Subject: Quick inputs for sizing the dedicated pool

Li — great to meet earlier. To draft a clear onramp plan we need the following so our slab math is concrete:

1) Confirm average and peak token volumes (daily or monthly). You mentioned ~30M tokens/day as a target — confirm if that is net of cached prefixes.
2) Distribution of request sizes: median tokens per request, 90th percentile, and percent of >1000-token calls.
3) SLA targets: p95 interactive latency target and any hard p99 caps.
4) Expected pilot start date and acceptable committed GPUs for Q3 procurement cycles.

I attached a tiny calc you can edit. If you prefer, drop a sanitized sample day and we
'll run a peak-run simulation.

Regards,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: stratus_throughput_calc.xlsx (Excel, 45 KB)

From: Li Wei <li.wei@stratus.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@stratus.ai>
Date: 2028-05-01T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick inputs for sizing the dedicated pool

Ben —

Answers inline:
- Average: 30,000,000 tokens/day (Q3 target). This is raw tokens; we estimate ~10% prefix reuse at the moment.
- Typical request: mean ~120 tokens, 90th ~850 tokens, ~10% > 1000 tokens.
- SLA: p95 <= 450 ms for interactive endpoints; p99 goal < 1.5s but not contractually required for pilot.
- Pilot start: aiming 2028-07-01; procurement team prefers fixed SKU commit for first quarter.

We provided a sanitized CSV of a representative day in the drive folder. Please include warm/cold cache sensitivity in your recommendation.

Thanks,
Li
Head of Platform, Stratus AI

Attachment: stratus_sample_day.csv (CSV, 18 KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal calc: Stratus onramp sizing notes

Team — I ran their numbers in the calc and sketched two pragmatic onramp options. Summary:

- Baseline demand: 30M tokens/day -> sustained ~347 tps; peak hour (20% day) ~1,667 tps.
- Model throughput assumptions (profiles measured on our runtime):
  * 7B opt (A100 fp16 path): ~1,200 tps/GPU p95 450ms with 120-token outputs
  * 12B opt (H100 fp16 path): ~2,400 tps/GPU p95 450ms
- Cold-cache multiplier: expect 20% throughput reduction for first 90s after a cache miss.

Sizing options:
Option Conservative: 3x A100-80GB slab (2 serving + 1 spare) — supports peak with ~2x buffer and simple failover.
Option Lean: 1x H100 active with autoscale to 2x at 50% util — lower committed capex, relies on autoscale warmup and burst fallback lanes.

Operational asks for MAP: load-test plan (3-hr 1.5x peak), autoscale trigger guidance, and rollback playbook. I'll draft a short appendix with the per-sku curves for the call.

-Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_gpu_profiles.pdf (PDF, 620 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-03T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal calc: Stratus onramp sizing notes

Couple of technical points to include in the MAP:
- Autoscale warmup: typical slab spin-up is ~30-60s; first 2 minutes post-scale see higher p95 due to KV coldness. Recommend burst policy or pre-warmed hot spare.
- Acceptance test: replicate a 1.5x peak sustained for 3 hours and verify p95 <= 450ms; include warm/cold runs.
- Routing: prefer steering interactive traffic to the H100 slab when present; ensure token-rate conversions are explicit in routing rules to avoid over-committing cheaper SKUs.

I'll add model-level perf curves and worst-case multipliers to the appendix.

-Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachment: N/A

From: Li Wei <li.wei@stratus.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stratus.ai>
Date: 2028-05-04T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stratus AI dedicated onramp & slab sizing

Kim / Ben —

Thanks for the options and clear notes. We
re leaning toward the conservative path for Q3 to simplify our SLA commitments. Please prepare a one-page MAP with these specifics:
- Pilot start: 2028-07-01
- Committed slab: 3x A100-80GB (2 active + 1 spare)
- Acceptance test: 3-hr load test at 1.5x peak with p95 <= 450 ms
- Operational runbook: autoscale triggers, failover steps, and rollback to hosted fallback

Also provide a compact cost comparison vs the H100-lean path for our procurement review. Elena will follow up with contract timeline details.

Li Wei
Head of Platform, Stratus AI

Attachment: procurement_checklist.xlsx (Excel, 26 KB)
